title: Retrievability
content: Retrievability is a measure of how easily a retrieval system can return a given document across the range of queries the system receives.

meta.why: A page that a system rarely returns cannot be cited, however well the page is written.
meta.example: A page that describes its product with internal code names is returned for fewer buyer questions than a page that uses the buyers' own words.
meta.check: Search for your page using the varied phrasings buyers use and record which phrasings return it.
meta.limitation: We use retrievability as a concept from information retrieval research, and no AI search product reports a retrievability score for a page.
meta.sources: Azzopardi and Vinay: Retrievability, an evaluation measure for higher order information access tasks | https://doi.org/10.1145/1458082.1458157 | Research paper
